title: Canada public sector launch brief
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is the go-to-market brief for our targeted launch to Canadian public sector agencies (federal, provincial, and select municipal programs). It is intended for Sales, Solutions Engineering, Legal/Compliance, and Customer Success to align on messaging, target accounts, competitive posture, and an executable enablement checklist.

High-level launch objective:
- Enable ten active POC engagements with Canadian public agencies within 90 days of announcement, with at least two converting to pilot contracts (paid pilot / procurement pathway).
- Establish Redwood as a credible inference partner for workloads requiring local data residency and auditable key management.

Why Canada (opportunity thesis):
- Procurement tailwinds: Several provinces and the federal government have published AI guidance and procurement frameworks emphasizing data residency and supplier transparency — a clear fit for Redwood Private + Dedicated + KMS integrations.
- Market size: Multiple ministries and agencies evaluating generative AI for document automation, citizen services, and internal knowledge management offer an addressable market for inference-hosted + on-prem solutions.
- Competitive gap: Many vendors either offer pure cloud endpoints with limited residency guarantees or heavy managed-service integrations with long lead times. Redwood can differentiate with a packaged private deployment, shorter time to pilot, and a predictable pricing/operational model.

Target personas and use cases:
- CIO/IT Directors (provincial/federal): procurement, data residency, risk reduction. Key asks: vendor controls, certificates, uptime SLA, integration with existing identity/KMS systems.
- ML/AI Program Leads (innovation offices): want reproducible results, model version control, predictable latency for citizen-facing apps.
- Solutions/Platform Engineers: care about deployment templates, observability, rollbacks, and cost controls.
- Use cases to lead with: automated FOI/records summarization, multilingual citizen support (English/French), case triage for benefits programs, redaction and PII detection pipelines.

Core positioning statements (top-line):
- Headline: "Redwood Inference for Canada Public Sector: Local control, production-grade inference, and auditability without reengineering your stack."
- 2–3 line elevator: "Redwood provides a unified inference runtime that runs in your VPC or on-premise to meet Canadian residency and audit requirements, while delivering the same latency, cost controls, and rollout tools our public cloud customers use. Short pilots, predictable economics, and clear paths to production."

Key proof points to surface in outreach and collateral:
- Private/VPC deployment option with KMS/HSM integrations and customer-controlled keys.
- Model version pinning and rollout controls for auditable change management.
- Observability: per-route latency/cost, token-level traces, and native logging hooks for SOC/evidence collection.
- Deployment reference: a sandbox on-prem deployment completed with a provincial partner (internal case study template ready for sales demo).
- Security/compliance: ISO 27001 controls (company-level), SOC2 in process / roadmap, penetration testing report available for red-team requests.

Competitive landscape notes (short bullets):
- Major cloud vendors (GCP, Azure): offer managed model endpoints and can meet residency via local regions. Pros: deep integrations and procurement familiarity. Cons: bundled costs, limited model transparency, often single-vendor lock-in. Sales angle: Redwood offers multi-model neutrality, lighter procurement, and a packaged on-prem option that avoids full cloud migration debates.
- Large LLM-API providers (Vendor X/Y): simple hosted APIs but limited guarantees on residency and key controls. Sales angle: Redwood matches hosted ease but adds Private deployment and enterprise SLAs.
- Specialist inference vendors (Startups A/B): better performance tuning but often require significant professional services and bespoke ops. Sales angle: Redwood provides a repeatable deployment template, lower onboarding effort, and built-in tooling (rollouts, tracing, evals).

Elevator battlecard (quick ref for calls):
- Lead objection: "We already have cloud contracts or Cloud-First mandates."
  - Response: "We provide a VPC-first path that can sit inside your existing cloud region and integrate with your KMS — or for tighter controls, our on-prem appliance package. Either way, you keep control of keys, logs, and model versions."
- Lead objection: "Can you meet our procurement/cert requirements?"
  - Response: "We have a standard compliance packet for public sector buyers (security docs, SOC/pen test summaries, SLA templates); for Canada-specific asks we have a checklist and a predefined engagement with Legal to map to procurement templates."
- Lead objection: "How quickly can we pilot?"
  - Response: "Typical pilot timeline: 2–6 weeks for a VPC-based pilot; 6–12 weeks for an on-prem sandbox depending on procurement/ops constraints. We provide a concise pilot SOW and a turnkey engineering pathway."

Sample announcement / outreach snippets (can be adapted for email, press, and field play):
- Short subject line: "Announcing Redwood for Canadian public sector: local control for generative AI pilots"
- Email intro (customer-facing): "We’re launching a tailored package to help Canadian public agencies run production-grade LLM inference with controls needed for data residency and auditability. We’ll partner on pilots for document automation, citizen-facing assistants, and secure redaction pipelines."
- Internal slack/field note: "Heads up: Canada Public Sector launch materials are live. Use the "Canada Public Sector" kit for POC offers. For anyone engaging federal/provincial accounts, loop in Legal and Solutions Eng early."

Sales enablement assets to prepare (priority order):
1) Canada public sector one-pager (customer language + procurement checklist).
2) Technical pilot SOW template (VPC + on-prem variant).
3) Compliance packet (security controls, pen test summary, KMS diagram, sample SLA).
4) Solutions engineering runbook for a Montreal/Toronto sandbox (network diagrams, firewall rules, data flow).
5) Battlecards vs Azure and Vendor X (concise feature/price/ops differences).
6) Demo script showing French-English multilingual prompt pipeline and audit logs.

Launch checklist (field-ready):
- [ ] Legal: finalize Canada POC T&Cs and procurement clause templates.
- [ ] Security: complete a targeted pen test for the packaged on-prem installer and assemble compliance packet.
- [ ] Engineering: publish a Canada reference deployment (VPC region + sample infra-as-code).
- [ ] Solutions Eng: rehearse demo and pilot runbook; create runbook for common network/topology questions.
- [ ] Sales: update pricing sheet with public sector pilot discounts and procurement payment terms.
- [ ] Marketing: landing page + downloadable one-pager; PR outreach list for Canadian trade press and public-sector newsletters.

KPIs & success metrics for first 90 days:
- Number of leads sourced via public-sector outreach: 50
- POCs activated: 10
- Paid pilots/contracts signed: 2
- Demos run (Solutions Eng-led): 20
- Heatmap of interest by province: prioritize ON, QC, BC, and federal ministries focusing on citizen services

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: procurement cycles are slow and long.
  - Mitigation: prioritize smaller agencies and pilot-friendly programs; offer limited-scope paid pilots with clear success criteria.
- Risk: security/compliance questions stall conversations.
  - Mitigation: pre-pack compliance artifacts and a named Security point-of-contact to accelerate reviews.
- Risk: internal resource contention for on-prem installs.
  - Mitigation: emphasize VPC-hosted pilots where feasible and provide a clear engineering SOW for on-prem installations.

Next steps (owners and timeline):
- Sales: draft target account list and top outreach messages (owner: Liam O'Connor) — due 2025-02-24.
- Legal: POC T&C template and procurement clause (owner: Sofia Martinez) — due 2025-02-21.
- Security: finalize compliance packet and pen test summary (owner: Noah Kim) — due 2025-02-28.
- Engineering: publish Canada reference infra repo and pilot SRE on-call rotation (owner: Elena Rossi) — due 2025-03-07.

Appendix: quick FAQ for field reps (short answers)
- Q: Do you host customer data?
- A: Depends on the deployment. For Private/VPC and on-prem we do not persist customer data in our hosted systems; keys and logs can be stored in customer-managed KMS. Hosted API customers should consult the data residency table for region availability.
- Q: Can Redwood work with existing HSM/KMS vendors?
- A: Yes — we support standard KMS/HSM integrations and can exchange the crypto material required for key-wrapping.
- Q: What models do you support in Private installs?
- A: We certify a set of open and licensed models for Private and Dedicated deployments; Solutions Eng will provide the current compatibility matrix during scoping.
- Q: What is required from our network team for an on-prem pilot?
- A: A small set of firewall exceptions and an admin user with console access. Full network runbook is in the playbook asset.

Notes to self / open questions:
- Coordinate with Marketing on a bilingual (EN/FR) one-pager for major provinces; prioritize French translations for QC.
- Chase SOC2 timeline and consider a short note in the packet: "SOC2 in progress — expected Q3 2025."
- Confirm whether we can provide a sandbox in Montréal region for VPC demos (Ops action).

End of brief.
